records.name: More Pass Plus Learning Center
records.summary: Offers workshops, trainings and resources to parents, caregivers and families, with a focus on learning and family life. The site lists no upcoming sessions, so ask the group when the next one is.
records.what_you_do: Email or call the group to ask about upcoming workshops, or to volunteer, mentor, sponsor, or share your professional skills in its trainings.

schedule.text: No upcoming workshop dates are posted on the site. Ask the group when the next session is.

first_step.how: Email morepassplus3@gmail.com, or use the contact form on morepassplus.com, and ask about the next workshop or training.
first_step.basis: Workshops and trainings are aimed at parents and families, and the site gives an email, a phone number and a contact form. It lists no upcoming sessions or sign-up steps, so the way in is clear but the timing is not.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical session, how long it runs, or what it costs. It says the group offers trainings and workshops both in person and online, along with resources for families.

records.notes: Dormant: the newest dated items on the site are from August 2023 (a career fair on Aug 3, 2023 and a community restoration day on Aug 23, 2023). The programs page lists older events from 2022 and 2023 only, and its Upcoming heading shows a Black History Month celebration with no year. Tier 1 had probably_active with no date. The homepage links a post dated 2026/07/16, but that link appears only inside a login URL, so it was not counted. The library page lists books for STAR series participants and has no dates. The group still publishes a working email, phone and contact form, so the owner may want to decide whether a dormant group stays listed.

records.name: 12 Plus
records.summary: A college and career readiness nonprofit that works inside partner Philadelphia high schools, helping students plan for college and jobs after 12th grade.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers can sit on panels at the yearly career and higher education fairs, act as mock interview partners, or present at information sessions. Working professionals can also apply to the 10-month Fellows program, which places fellows full time in school-based centers.

schedule.text: No set weekly schedule for volunteers. The career and higher education fairs run once a year at the group's centers, and volunteers are asked to take on at least one opportunity a year.

cost.text: No fee to volunteer is listed. The group asks for donations, which are tax deductible.

first_step.how: Email info@12plus.org to say which role interests you, such as a career fair panelist or a mock interview partner. There is no form to fill out.
first_step.basis: Volunteer roles are listed publicly with a clear email contact and no minimum monthly commitment. The site does not describe training or screening.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a visit takes. Volunteers can serve as panelists at the yearly career and college fairs, as mock interview partners for students or alumni, or at information sessions. You are asked to take on at least one opportunity a year, and there is no volunteer fee.

records.notes: The fellowship page says the group is accepting applications for the 2026 to 2027 Fellows class. No month is shown, so the status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is recorded. The Fellows program is 10 months, full time in school-based PLUS Centers in Philadelphia and Camden. Pay and the application deadline are not stated. The volunteer page lists no training or background check. The home page says the group works with 15 high schools this year. The only year on the other pages is in the copyright footer, which is not used as evidence.

records.name: 21st Ward 4th of July Association
records.summary: Runs a neighborhood Independence Day parade in Northwest Philadelphia that the group says dates back to 1831, with a park party and veterans events through the year.
records.what_you_do: Watch the July 4 parade or join the veterans concert and picnic at Gorgas Park. To march, email the association first: the participants listed on the site are churches, veterans and Masonic groups, among others, and special units need advance approval.

schedule.text: The parade runs each July 4, starting at 9 a.m. The association also holds a park party in Gorgas Park and a yearly veterans concert and picnic there.

locations.label: Gorgas Park (park party and veterans events)

cost.text: The veterans concert and picnic is free to attend. The site lists no fee for the parade or the park party, and merchandise is sold at the park party.

first_step.how: Watch the July 4 parade, or come to the veterans concert and picnic at Gorgas Park. To march, email 21stward4thjuly@gmail.com after reading the Participants and Parade Rules pages.
first_step.basis: Watching the parade and the public park events is open to anyone. The pages give no steps for joining a parade unit beyond an email, and special units need advance approval, so the way in to marching is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The parade starts at 9 a.m. on July 4. The veterans concert and picnic features a concert band, classic cars, a costumed mascot and a live bald eagle, food for sale, and activities for children on the Gorgas Park playground. Anyone can attend, and the page does not say how long the parade lasts.
first_visit_tips: If you are a veteran, arrive before 10 a.m. at the veterans event.
Marchers: bicycles, motor vehicles and special units need advance approval, and throwing candy or other items to the crowd is banned.
Email the association with questions at 21stward4thjuly@gmail.com.

records.notes: The Gorgas Park party page says the July 4, 2026 party (11 a.m. to 1 p.m.) was postponed for a heat advisory, with no new date. The home page calls the 2026 events a success. The party is recorded as postponed, so check before going. The veterans page gives Gorgas Park at 6300 Ridge Ave, says the next concert is on July 31, 2027, and says veteran and organization registration for 2026 is closed until 2027. The parade map is not in the page text, so the start point and route are not recorded. Church marshals report to the Grand Parade Marshal at Manayunk and Lyceum Avenues. Friends of Gorgas Park is named as the party host and is listed under leads_only. Performers and vendors at the veterans event were not followed. The parade rules point to a PDF with more detail, which was not read.

records.name: A New Dawn
records.summary: A Mill Creek-Parkside nonprofit that turns vacant lots into gardens, greenhouses and gathering places. It grows food through farming and hydroponics and runs wellness and hands-on STEAM skill building for youth, families and seniors.
records.what_you_do: Join one of the listed sessions, such as a Saturday midday session at the Tiffany Fletcher Recreation Center, or email support@anewdawnincorporated.org to ask about the garden and programs. Donations are accepted.

schedule.text: Sessions repeat through the week at the Tiffany Fletcher Recreation Center, the Lucien E. Blackwell Center and a site on Wyalusing Avenue. They run on several weekdays and Saturdays, mostly in the afternoon and evening. The events page does not say what each session covers or whether registration is needed.

first_step.how: Pick a session on the events page and go to that center. The page does not say whether you need to register, so email support@anewdawnincorporated.org or call 267-277-3069 before your first visit.
first_step.basis: Sessions are listed publicly with days, times and places, but the page does not say who each one is for or whether you must register, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a session runs, what it costs, or what a newcomer does first. Its about page describes hands-on farming and hydroponics, wellness and skill building for youth, families and seniors, and canning and nutrition workshops taught by the group's president.

records.notes: Correction: the tier 1 line about asking for garden plots through the Plot Information link is not supported. That link leads to a page with no plot details, so the claim is removed. That page does list a contact address (4837 to 59 Aspen Street), a phone number and an email, which are added. The events page shows sessions with no year, so no year is recorded. A Saturday noon run from October 3 to November 21 is left out of the schedule because it is a dated run. Several past events are marked Event Ended with no names or dates. The STEAM wording comes from the home page. Aspen Farms is listed at 4837 Aspen Street on the events page.

records.name: Academy of Natural Sciences volunteer program (Drexel University)
records.summary: The Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University recruits adult and teen volunteers for its collections, labs, bird collision monitoring and nature walks. Most roles need a steady weekly schedule for at least a year.
records.what_you_do: Help with specimen collections or lab support, monitor for birds hurt by building collisions and transport them, or support nature walks and community science projects.

schedule.text: Regular weekly shifts, mostly on weekdays. Collections roles run weekdays 9 am to 5 pm. Bird collision monitoring runs April to May and September to November.

locations.label: Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University, Philadelphia

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer application linked from the Academy's volunteer page, then email volunteers@ansp.org about open roles. The application runs through an outside volunteer-management system.
first_step.basis: An online application and a commitment of at least a year on a regular weekly shift come first. The steps are clear, but the page describes no orientation or training.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a regular shift of half a day to several days a week for at least a year. Collections assistants work in departments such as botany, entomology, ornithology and the library, on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm, and lab volunteers support the Patrick Center for Environmental Research. The page does not mention training, orientation or fees.

records.notes: The Academy's own volunteer pages are current, but the newest dated item found is a journal article from April 2022 (from its URL path), so the status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is recorded. The application is hosted on an outside system (Volgistics). The Academy street address was not on the pages read, so none was added. The Bird Safe Philly and Lights Out Philly volunteer page is linked from the Academy but has no URL in the page text, so it was not followed. One Nature at Noon link returned a not-found page, so the Nature at Noon details come from the sign-up page.

records.name: Achieveability
records.summary: A West Philadelphia nonprofit that works to lift families out of poverty through education, affordable housing, and support services. It runs family programs and invites volunteers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer for office support, skills workshops, tax help, resume feedback, house makeovers, block cleanups or donation drives. You can also ask about its family programs, such as the Family Self-Sufficiency Program, which has strict eligibility rules.

schedule.text: The main office is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 5 pm. Community events are on hold for now, so ask about volunteer roles by email or phone.

cost.text: No program or volunteer fees are listed on the pages read. The site takes donations.

first_step.how: Email development@achieve-ability.org or call 215-748-8800 to ask which volunteer role fits your schedule, such as front desk help, a skills workshop or a block cleanup.
first_step.basis: Volunteer roles are listed with a phone number, an email and an office address, and no application or fee is named. The pages do not state a time commitment or whether training is given.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a volunteer shift lasts or whether training is given. Roles range from answering calls and running the front desk to leading workshops on budgeting or parenting, helping prepare tax returns, and joining house makeovers or block cleanups.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go on a Friday, because the site lists different Friday hours in two places.

records.notes: Impact Day is listed on the events page as Friday, April 24, 2026. The page labels it upcoming, but the date has passed as of 2026-10-08, so it is the newest dated evidence. The volunteer page says community events are on hold. The Family Self-Sufficiency Program has strict eligibility: an adult with a child under 18, enrolled or planning to enroll in post-secondary school, a work requirement of 30 or more hours a week, a minimum household income of $1,500 a month, and housing conditions. It is not open enrollment. The WorkSmart West Philly page does not say whether the program costs anything. The Friday office hours conflict (the page says virtual 9 am to 5 pm, the footer says 9 am to 1 pm). The volunteer email (development) differs from the general email on the homepage, so both are recorded.

records.name: AfterShock Fam
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs music and arts workshops for kids, including DJ, beatmaking and music production camps, and pairs young people with one-on-one mentors. It also connects artists who want to mentor.
records.what_you_do: Kids can join the NoChaser Kidz DJ Cafe, a Wednesday workshop in music and art, or ask about the summer music camps. Kids who have attended a workshop can be matched with online one-on-one mentoring, and artists can join the Creative Network after mentor training.

schedule.text: The NoChaser Kidz DJ Cafe meets on Wednesdays. The site lists music camps for ages 8 to 16 in July, with no year shown, and no current session dates are posted.

locations.label: Lancaster Avenue site (listed for DJ Cafe sessions)

cost.text: No prices are listed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the online registration form on the NoChaser website, or contact the NoChaser team, and confirm the current session dates before you sign up.
first_step.basis: The DJ Cafe is open to kids interested in music and art regardless of experience, and families are told to register online. The only dated sessions shown are from 2024, so check that it is running.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions are on Wednesdays, and the page gives no start or end times. Kids learn the basics of DJing, such as mixing, scratching and beat juggling, and work on music and art projects. The page lists no fee, and sessions may be held at community centers or schools instead of the Lancaster Avenue address.

records.notes: The newest dated evidence is the DJ Cafe Wednesday list from October to December 2024, so the status is probably_active (12 to 24 months old). The events page lists only one placeholder entry titled Test with no date, so it was not used. The contact page had no contact details in the capture, so only the tier 1 contact person is kept. BeatCamp (July, ages 8 to 16, limited to 20 campers) is a week at YMCA Camp Shady Brook, which the page places in Colorado, so it is not a local option. Camp Boredomfighters is a week-long retreat run with the same camp. The partners page was not followed. The dated sessions use a 2024 year on the page.

leads_only.name: Friends of Gorgas Park
leads_only.note: Named on the association's Gorgas Park page as the group behind the July 4 park party. No own website was found on that page, so it was not checked further.

notes: Seven groups, all with working own websites. Used 30 of 60 fetches and 0 of 1 WebSearch, because each group's own pages were reachable from the home page links. No rate limiting seen. Status changes: More Pass Plus moved to dormant (newest dated item is August 2023). Achieveability moved to active on an April 2026 event. 21st Ward confirmed active (rules updated June 20, 2026, and the 2026 parade). 12 Plus and AfterShock stay probably_active. Corrections: the A New Dawn garden plot claim was removed, and its email and phone were added from its contact page. Veterans event vendors and performers, a Nature at Noon link on the Academy site (not found), and the Academy's Bird Safe Philly page were not followed. All seven records are publish verdicts.
